entries.note: The claim attributes a private understanding deficit to an ego-related mental block. Public technical statements cannot establish that psychological explanation.

entries.test: Public architectural descriptions and formal-reasoning demonstrations could test whether world models require the specified explicit, structured, directly retrievable knowledge.
entries.note: This asserts a technical necessity, with an explicit qualification about his 2020 article. A demonstrated counterexample could refute that necessity.

entries.test: Public architecture disclosures and independent reliability evaluations could establish whether AI can operate trustworthily without contributions from both neural and symbolic traditions.
entries.note: He asserts a necessary technical ingredient, rather than merely recommending a research direction. Trustworthy AI has broad scope, but the necessity claim admits empirical counterexamples.

entries.test: Meta's public research records, team information, JEPA publications and demonstrated outputs through January 6, 2026 could establish the project's duration, approximate staffing and whether its output amounted to only a handful of papers.
entries.note: The duration, staffing and limited-output assertions are checkable. Whether the papers are earth-shaking is an evaluative gloss.
Calling the name right and the implementation inadequate expresses an assessment of worth without a specified adequacy threshold.
The central commitment is that the field desperately needs this kind of exploration. Evidence about technical novelty cannot settle that judgment.
